subject: Re: Burst capacity voucher provisioning for FinOne POC load run
messages:
From: Natalie Brooks <natalie@finone.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finone.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: burst capacity for FinOne POC load run

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week — the latency numbers looked promising. We have a 72-hour end‑to‑end load run planned to validate tail‑latency under concurrency for our search use case. The test window we're targeting is Jun 18–20 (UTC).

Quick ask: could Redwood provision a temporary burst voucher/credit and a short SLA note so we can hit realistic traffic (expected peak ~220 qps, sustained ~90 qps, peak concurrency ~3400 concurrent requests) without hitting trial caps? We want to run three full regressions and smoke checks during the window. Acceptance criteria: p99 < 450ms and no systemic errors >0.5%.

I attached the test-plan spreadsheet with expected token estimates and the MOP summary. Let me know if you need a PO or procurement contact — I cc'd procurement.

Thanks,
Natalie Brooks
Head of Platform Engineering
FinOne

Attachment: FinOne-POC-TestPlan.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Brooks <natalie@finone.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: burst capacity for FinOne POC load run

Hi Natalie — great to hear the demo was useful. We're happy to support the e2e run. A few quick clarifying items so we can size a voucher appropriately:

- Exact start/end UTC window (we prefer to lock the window to avoid cross‑tenant contention).
- Expected total token consumption per regression (your spreadsheet helps but please confirm the conservative estimate).
- Primary billing contact and whether a PO is required before provisioning.
- Any restricted data or VPC requirements for the test.

Proposed path: we can provision a provisional burst voucher for a 72‑hour window and a short written addendum (voucher agreement) that lists rollback and rate limits. Typical vouchers we issue for these e2e runs are in the 100k–200k token range depending on concurrency and sequence lengths. If you can confirm the numbers, I'll route for approval and attach a voucher agreement draft for signature.

Cc'ing Jordan and Marcus to align on quota and on‑call coverage.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: voucher-agreement-draft.pdf (draft), poc-mop.docx (MOP brief)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: FinOne voucher ask — recommendation

Team — forwarding Natalie’s request (below). She’s asking for a 72‑hour burst run Jun 18–20 with estimated peaks as noted. The spreadsheet estimates ~140k tokens per full regression; given three regressions + buffers, I'm recommending we provision a 150,000 token voucher for the 72‑hour window with the following constraints:

- Voucher valid Jun 18 00:00 UTC -> Jun 20 23:59 UTC
- Hard rate limit: 500 qps per org across the voucher window; canary policy to throttle by 50% first hour
- On‑call tracer: Marcus to be primary for hotspots; Jordan to own canary rollback trigger
- Require procurement signoff or PO for invoicing after voucher use (deal FIN-40123)

Risks: if tests spike above estimates we may affect other tenants during noisy hours; recommend a canary + immediate rollback if error rate >0.5% or p99 >800ms. Requesting quick approvals so I can generate the voucher and the DocuSign envelope.

Jordan — you comfortable with 150k and the rollback policy? Marcus — can you confirm on‑call availability for Jun 18–20? Laura / Aditya — any finance/legal objections to the short voucher addendum?

+1 on 150k token voucher and the canary rollback plan.
Please include a clause that requires automatic circuit‑breaker if error rate >0.5% for >5 minutes and that the canary throttles to 50% of requested qps for first hour. Finance is okay to bill post‑run for vouchers tied to deal FIN-40123 — Laura, thanks for the quick check.

Marcus — please confirm you'll be on rotation for Jun 18–20 and ensure tracing is enabled for their org (request ticket to infra team if needed).

-Jordan

Hi Natalie — thanks for the details. We’ve provisioned a 150,000 token voucher tied to deal FIN-40123 and created a DocuSign addendum outlining the canary rollback policy and tracing obligations. Voucher token: VCHR-7F3K-LM (redeemable Jun 18 00:00 UTC -> Jun 20 23:59 UTC).

What we’ve included:
- 150k tokens, one‑time use within window
- Canary: first hour throttled to 50% of requested qps, automatic rollback if error rate >0.5% for 5m or p99 >800ms
- Marcus will be on on‑call for hotspots and will have tracing hooks enabled
- Post‑run invoicing: we’ll bill against the PO or procurement contact you provided (procurement@finone.com)

Please review the DocuSign here: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123FIN and sign the voucher addendum. I attached the voucher invoice/record for your finance team.

Can we do a quick pre‑run sync on Jun 17 at 16:00 UTC to walk through the canary plan and confirm test timing? If that works, I’ll send an invite.
